messages:
anya: Quick postmortem follow-ups from last night's KV-cache OOM. Root cause looks like sticky residency growth + lots of small fragment allocations in the write path. I'm listing actions below, please ack and claim ownership. Short bullets only here; we'll track details in the ticket.

mike: Ack. I'll take the short-term mitigation: re-enable softlimit (10% headroom) + immediate eviction policy rollback to LRU-approx. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

leigh: Ack. I'll own profiling and reproducibility. Plan: run heap sampling on canaries + full pprof/heapdump from impacted hosts. Posting commands I used last night.

leigh: ```sh
# run on canary node
sudo systemctl restart redis-serving
./heap-hr --sample-duration=60s --interval=10s --output=/tmp/heap-sample-$(date +%s).pb
# upload to s3 for analysis
aws s3 cp /tmp/heap-sample-*.pb s3://redwood-ops/kv-leak-profiles/
```

anya: Nice. Add a note to capture "alloc-site" labels in heap-hr output so we can correlate with code paths. Also add one-off trace for GC pauses.

sriram: I'll take the GC/allocator tuning work. Short plan: 1) increase GC pressure threshold on canaries, 2) enable deferred-sweep for 48h experiment, 3) monitor pause times. Will create the RFC and link.

mike: Quick mitigation checklist I'm applying now: 1) softlimit + eviction rollback, 2) enforce per-shard mem caps with -X softprobe, 3) enable higher eviction frequency for hot shards. Pushing a canary in 15m; will post deploy status. :rocket:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started by mike (deploy/kv-served v3.2.1-canary).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment succeeded on 3/3 hosts (mike). :white_check_mark:

leigh: Initial canary heap-samples uploaded: s3://redwood-ops/kv-leak-profiles/1769001300-*.pb. Early signal: high allocation sites in shards/put_batch path and buffer pooling not being reclaimed.

anya: Good catch. For ownership: mike = short-term mitigation + canary rollout, leigh = profiling & artifacts + timeline, sriram = GC/allocator tuning + RFC, anya = long-term refactor (shard cache lifecycle and pool redesign).

mike: timeline: mitigation done on canaries now, rolling to 20% prod tomorrow 09:00PT if no regressions. Will post canary metrics (residency, p99 latency, OOM rate) every 2h in this thread.

leigh: Profiling cadence: heap-hr samples at 09:15, 11:15, 13:15 PT tomorrow. I'll attach diffs.

sriram: RFC draft by EOD Friday. If tuning buys us stability, we'll schedule a follow-up canary for the allocator flags next week.

anya: Also action: create a recurring monthly "kv-residency health" check in ops calendar + add a dashboard that surfaces frag ratio, small-alloc rate, and eviction churn. Owner: leigh (dash) + mike (alerts).

mike: Added alert: frag_ratio > 0.35 for 10m OR small_alloc_rate spike > 2000/min triggers page (prod-ops).

leigh: Note for postmortem doc: include the pprof snippet and the exact heap-hr flags we used; I'll update the ticket with artifacts and short audio notes from the debug session.

anya: One last recurring pattern item: this OOM looks similar to February incident but with a slower growth curve. Please correlate both incidents in the PM doc (ticket #PI-2472).

mike: Acknowledged, linking graphs.

sriram: If we get sustained improvements from softlimit + GC flags, let's avoid quick refactor sprints and instead schedule a measured rewrite with benchmarks.

anya: Thanks all. If anyone else wants to pick up sub-tasks (eviction telemetry, synthetic load tests, postmortem writeup), add a short comment here with ETA. I'll compile and push to the postmortem ticket later today. :memo:

leigh: I'll add synthetic load tests (small-allocation skew) to testgrid; ETA Mon.

mike: I'll take eviction telemetry (per-shard evict counters + residency heatmap) — ETA Thu.

infra-bot: reminder-bot: Incident ticket PI-2472 updated with follow-ups and owners.

anya: closing thread for now; we'll use this thread for quick updates only. Full writeup in PI-2472. :eyes:
